proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted draw.  By the definition of \(F_G(A)\), every \(i\in A\) and \(j\in C\subseteq F_G(A)\) satisfy
\[
\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)>2. \tag{1}
\]
The arm swap either gives \((T,C_0)=(A,C)\) or \((T,C_0)=(C,A)\), so (1) holds for every \(i\in T\) and \(j\in C_0\).  Edges of \(H_G\) join only opposite-arm vertices, and an opposite-arm pair \((i,1),(j,0)\) is an edge exactly when \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\), by \(\text{def:gate-conflict-graph}\).  Hence no two vertices of
\[
(T\times\{1\})\cup(C_0\times\{0\})
\]
are adjacent, proving stability.

If a vertex \(v\) belonged to both \(\bigcup_{i\in T}N_G[i]\) and \(\bigcup_{j\in C_0}N_G[j]\), then for some \(i\in T\) and \(j\in C_0\),
\[
\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)
\le \operatorname{dist}_G(i,v)+\operatorname{dist}_G(v,j)
\le2,
\]
contradicting (1).  Thus the two forced-neighborhood unions are disjoint, so the assignment in \(\text{def:reservoir-capsule}\) is well defined.  For \(i\in T\), it has \(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}|_{N_G[i]}=\boldsymbol 1|_{N_G[i]}\).  Assumption \(\text{ass:ani}\) therefore gives
\[
y_i(Z^{\mathrm{cap}})=y_i(\boldsymbol 1)=y_{i1}.
\]
The identical argument with zeros gives \(y_i(Z^{\mathrm{cap}})=y_{i0}\) for every \(i\in C_0\).  This proves all three assertions.

Condition throughout on the revealed graph \(G\), and suppose \(\pi_u>0\) for all \(u\in\mathcal U\).  Proposition \(\text{prop:capsule-realization}\) shows that whenever \(X_{(i,a)}=1\), the realized data contain the endpoint value \(y_{ia}\).  By the definition of \(\pi_u\),
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{X_u}{\pi_u}\,\middle|\,G\right]=1. \tag{2}
\]
Using (2), the definition of \(\widetilde\tau_G\), and the finite nature of the sum,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E[\widetilde\tau_G\mid G]
&=\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}s_a y_{ia}
  \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{X_{(i,a)}}{\pi_{(i,a)}}\,\middle|\,G\right]\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}(y_{i1}-y_{i0})
=\tau_G(y). \tag{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(Y\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal U}\) denote the endpoint vector with coordinate \(Y_{(i,a)}=y_{ia}\).  Expanding the variance in (3) coordinate by coordinate and applying \(\text{def:normalized-kernel}\) gives the exact identity
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde\tau_G\mid G)
=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{u,v\in\mathcal U}Y_u(\Gamma_G)_{uv}Y_v
=\frac1{n^2}Y^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_GY. \tag{4}
\]
The matrix \(\Gamma_G\) is positive semidefinite: if \(S\) is the diagonal matrix with \(S_{(i,a),(i,a)}=s_a\), then
\[
\Gamma_G=S\operatorname{Cov}\!\left((X_u/\pi_u)_{u\in\mathcal U}\mid G\right)S,
\]
and congruence by \(S\) preserves positive semidefiniteness.  The two endpoint moment restrictions in \(\text{def:endpoint-class}\), equivalently assumptions \(\text{ass:treated-endpoint-l2}\) and \(\text{ass:control-endpoint-l2}\), yield
\[
\|Y\|_2^2=\sum_{i\in V}y_{i1}^2+\sum_{i\in V}y_{i0}^2\le2n. \tag{5}
\]
Equations (4)--(5) and the Rayleigh-quotient inequality imply
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde\tau_G\mid G)
\le \frac{\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|Y\|_2^2}{n^2}
\le \frac{2\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}. \tag{6}
\]

Let \(\mathcal O=\sigma(G,Z^{\mathrm{cap}},y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}))\).  By \(\text{def:observed-estimator}\), \(\widehat\tau_G=\mathbb E[\widetilde\tau_G\mid\mathcal O]\).  Iterated expectation and (3) give \(\mathbb E[\widehat\tau_G\mid G]=\tau_G(y)\).  The conditional variance decomposition gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde\tau_G\mid G)
=\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\tau_G\mid G)
+\mathbb E[\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde\tau_G\mid\mathcal O)\mid G]
\ge \operatorname{Var}(\widehat\tau_G\mid G). \tag{7}
\]
Both estimators are unbiased, so their conditional mean squared errors equal their conditional variances.  Combining (6) and (7) proves the claimed inequalities.

Fix a finite revealed graph \(G\).  One trial samples a uniform \(k\)-subset, computes its radius-two forbidden union by at most \(k\) breadth-first searches of depth two, and checks whether the remaining set has at least \(k\) vertices.  After at most \(n^3\) trials, drawing \(C\), the arm-swap coin, and at most \(n\) remaining fair coins also takes polynomially many elementary operations.  Thus an exact sample from \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) is produced in time polynomial in \(n\) (and hence in \(n\) and \(d\)).

For exact finite evaluation, let \(\Omega_G\) be the finite latent sample space consisting of the ordered list of at most \(n^3\) proposed reservoirs, the accepted reservoir and \(C\) when acceptance occurs, the arm-swap coin, and the remaining assignment coins.  Every atom \(\eta\in\Omega_G\) has an explicitly known rational probability under \(\text{def:reservoir-capsule}\), and the maps
\[
\eta\longmapsto Z^{\mathrm{cap}}(\eta),\qquad
\eta\longmapsto X_u(\eta)
\]
are deterministic.  Consequently the finite sums
\[
\pi_u=\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G}\Pr(\eta\mid G)X_u(\eta)
\]
and
\[
\Pr(X_u=X_v=1\mid G)
=\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G}\Pr(\eta\mid G)X_u(\eta)X_v(\eta)
\]
compute every inclusion probability and, through \(\text{def:normalized-kernel}\), every entry of \(\Gamma_G\) exactly.  This enumeration is finite, although it is not asserted to be polynomial-time.

Finally fix an observed atom \(o=(G,z,y(z))\), and let
\[
\Omega_G(o)=\{\eta\in\Omega_G:(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}(\eta),y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}(\eta)))=(z,y(z))\}.
\]
Proposition \(\text{prop:capsule-realization}\) ensures that every endpoint appearing in \(\widetilde\tau_G(\eta)\) for \(\eta\in\Omega_G(o)\) is among the observed coordinates in \(o\).  Hence
\[
\widehat\tau_G(o)
=\frac{\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G(o)}\Pr(\eta\mid G)\widetilde\tau_G(\eta)}
       {\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G(o)}\Pr(\eta\mid G)} \tag{8}
\]
is an explicit finite sum whenever the denominator is positive; it is positive for every realized observation.  Equation (8) computes the Rao--Blackwell conditional weights using only \(G,z,y(z)\), not the unobserved focal metadata.  This proves totality and exact finite evaluability.

When \(d=0\), \(N_G[i]=\{i\}\), and for every \(k\)-set \(A\) one has \(F_G(A)=V\setminus A\).  Since \(k\le n/4\), every trial is accepted and \(C\) is a uniform \(k\)-subset of the complement of \(A\).  The arm swap makes each of \(T,C_0\) marginally uniform among \(k\)-subsets, and they are disjoint.  The remaining \(n-2k\) units receive independent fair coins by \(\text{def:reservoir-capsule}\).

Here \(\pi_{(i,a)}=k/n\), and \(\text{def:raw-estimator}\) becomes
\[
\widetilde\tau_G=\frac1k\sum_{i\in T}y_{i1}-\frac1k\sum_{i\in C_0}y_{i0}. \tag{27}
\]
Each term in (27) is an unbiased simple-random-sample mean.  For a fixed vector \((x_i)\) and a uniform \(k\)-subset \(S\), direct inclusion-probability algebra gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(k^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}x_i\right)
=\frac{n-k}{k(n-1)}\left\{\frac1n\sum_i(x_i-\bar x)^2\right\}. \tag{28}
\]
The endpoint moment bounds make each brace in (28) at most one.  Applying \(\operatorname{Var}(U-V)\le2\operatorname{Var}(U)+2\operatorname{Var}(V)\), and then Rao--Blackwell variance reduction from \(\text{lem:exact-risk-certificate}\), gives
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_G-\tau_G)^2\mid G]
\le \frac{4(n-k)}{k(n-1)}=O(n^{-1}),                           \tag{29}
\]
because \(k/n\to\log(2)/32>0\).

For the matching lower bound, every assignment exposes exactly one endpoint per unit, so the two exposure counts sum to \(n\) and their minimum is at most \(t=\lceil n/2\rceil\).  Independently in each arm, draw a fair sign \(B_a\), and conditional on it draw independent endpoint signs \(\xi_{ia}\) having mean \(B_a/(2\sqrt t)\).  This prior is supported on the endpoint \(L^2\) ball because \(\xi_{ia}^2=1\).  Define each non-endpoint potential outcome to be zero; since \(N_G[i]=\{i\}\), this produces an ANI schedule.  If the less-exposed arm has \(m\le t\) observations, the affinity between the laws of those observations under \(B_a=1\) and \(B_a=-1\) is
\[
\left(1-\frac1{4t}\right)^{m/2}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz therefore bounds their total variation by
\[
\sqrt{1-\left(1-\frac1{4t}\right)^m}\le\frac12.
\]
The expected posterior variance of \(B_a\) is consequently at least \(1/2\).  At least \(n-t\ge(n-1)/2\) endpoint signs in that arm remain unobserved, so the posterior variance of their contribution to the arm mean is at least
\[
\frac{(n-t)^2}{n^2}\frac1{4t}\frac12\ge\frac{c}{n}.
\]
Conditional expectation minimizes squared error; hence every outcome-independent design and every estimator has Bayes, and therefore worst-case, risk at least \(c/n\).  Thus \(R_2(G)\ge c/n\); (29) and \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\) give \(R_2(G)\le C/n\).

For the required smallest-instance check, if \(n=4\) then \(k=1\).  The capsule chooses one treated focal unit, one distinct control focal unit, and fair-coins the other two.  Hence the total treated count has law \(1+\operatorname{Binomial}(2,1/2)\), supported on \(\{1,2,3\}\), rather than being fixed at two.  Enumeration of the twelve ordered focal pairs and both arm labels verifies (27) is unbiased, but refutes the original description as a standard fixed balanced two-arm assignment.  This is exactly why the statement has been narrowed while retaining its valid rate assertion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: When \(d=0\), the capsule accepts immediately, selects two disjoint uniform fixed-size samples, labels them by the arm-swap coin, and assigns independent fair coins to the remaining units.  Its raw estimator is the difference of the corresponding endpoint sample means, its Rao--Blackwellization has worst-case risk \(O(n^{-1})\), and the unrestricted minimax risk satisfies \(R_2(G)=\Theta(n^{-1})\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original rate assertion is correct, but the claim that the capsule becomes the standard fixed balanced two-arm assignment is false.  At the exact stress test \(n=4,d=0,k=1\), its treated count is \(1+\operatorname{Binomial}(2,1/2)\), not identically two.  The proposed statement removes only that false identification, states the actual assignment law, and retains the proved capsule upper bound and unrestricted \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) minimax conclusion.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove, uniformly for a typical simple random \(d\)-regular graph, that the covariance operator of the accepted, symmetrized reservoir pair has norm \(O(n/k)\), together with uniform two-sided inclusion probabilities and the stated single-trial acceptance tail.
open_obligations.obstruction: The diagonal and same-arm simple-random-sampling scales are \(n/k\), but the opposite-arm block contains the radius-two incompatibility matrix.  Its constant mode must be canceled by the compatible-pair probabilities.  Acceptance conditioning and the random denominator \(\binom{|F_G(A)|}{k}\) make that cancellation nonexact, and the frozen primitives contain no mixing, switching, or spectral estimate controlling the residual operator.  Treating the asserted kernel bound as a lemma would assume the theorem's novel crux.
open_obligations.attempted: I expanded the signed covariance blockwise, used fixed arm sizes to identify the constant-mode cancellation in the uniform idealization, and tested diagonal, Schur, and centered distance-two spectral bounds.  Diagonal control proves necessity of the \(n/k\) scale; Schur control leaves an \(O(d^2)\) term and therefore misses the required logarithmic improvement.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The signed kernel has the exact positive-semidefinite representation
\[
\Gamma_G=S\operatorname{Cov}((X_u/\pi_u)_{u\in\mathcal U}\mid G)S,
\]
and therefore
\[
\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ge
\max_{u\in\mathcal U}\left(\pi_u^{-1}-1\right).
\]
Thus the asserted order \(n/k\) is the smallest possible order once \(\pi_u\asymp k/n\).  For an incompatible opposite-arm pair the unsigned normalized covariance equals \(-1\); after applying the contrast signs this contributes \(+1\).  Fixed arm sizes force cancellation of the constant cross-arm mode in the exactly uniform case, but proving that acceptance conditioning and the random set \(F_G(A)\) preserve this cancellation in operator norm requires a uniform switching or spectral estimate for the weighted compatible-pair kernel.  The elementary Schur bound controls it only at order \(d^2+n/k\), which is too large by the required factor \(\log(d+2)\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Close the risk upper bound without presuming the unresolved operator estimate in \(\text{thm:stable-kernel}\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact risk identity reduces the theorem to \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(n/k)\).  That is precisely the unresolved novel kernel assertion, so the logarithmic gain cannot be obtained from the current frozen primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: I derived the risk implication equation by equation and separately verified the \(\Theta(d^2)\) conflict-graph spectral comparison.  Replacing operator control by an entrywise or maximum-row-sum bound loses the factor \(\log(d+2)\).
open_obligations.partial_result:
On the event asserted by \(\text{thm:stable-kernel}\), \(\text{lem:exact-risk-certificate}\) gives immediately
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}\operatorname{MSE}(\widehat\tau_G\mid G)
\le \frac{2\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}
\le C\frac{(d+1)^2}{n\log(d+2)}=Cr(n,d).
\]
Independently, if \(B_G\) is the \(V\times V\) zero--one matrix of the relation \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\), then the adjacency matrix of \(H_G\) is \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&B_G\\B_G&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), so \(\lambda(H_G)=\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Every row sum is at most \(1+d^2\).  Under \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), the expected number of collisions among the \(d(d-1)\) length-two walks from a uniform vertex is \(O(d^4/n+d^2/n)=o(d^2)\); Markov's inequality shows that the average row sum is \((1-o_{\Pr}(1))d^2\).  The Rayleigh quotient at the all-ones vector and the maximum-row-sum bound then give \(\lambda(H_G)=\Theta_{\Pr}(d^2)\).  Hence only the unresolved covariance-kernel estimate prevents the full target proof.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Establish the upper half \(R_2(G)\le C r(n,d)\) needed to match the proved all-procedure converse.
open_obligations.obstruction: The lower half is proved in this dispatch, but the upper half depends on the unresolved stable-kernel operator estimate through \(\text{thm:capsule-upper}\).
open_obligations.attempted: I intersected the random-graph events and checked the minimax comparison.  This closes mechanically once the kernel theorem is available, but no independent route to its logarithmic upper rate follows from the frozen core.
open_obligations.partial_result: The all-procedure half is proved here: with probability \(1-o(1)\), \(R_2(G)\ge c r(n,d)\).  If the unresolved bound in \(\text{thm:stable-kernel}\) is established, the displayed calculation in the partial result for \(\text{thm:capsule-upper}\), together with the fact that \((\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}},\widehat\tau_G)\) is one admissible pair in \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\), gives \(R_2(G)\le Cr(n,d)\) on the same event.  Intersecting the two events then yields the stated matched frontier.  No lower-bound issue remains.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a polynomial-time observable approximation to the Rao--Blackwell weights and an operator-norm risk certificate with uniform \(o(r(n,d))\) error.
open_obligations.obstruction: Finite enumeration is exact but exponential.  Pointwise Monte Carlo evaluation of inclusions or covariance entries does not furnish the relative and operator-norm accuracy needed uniformly over the endpoint \(L^2\) ball, and the frozen handle supplies no contraction, mixing-time, or approximate-counting guarantee.
open_obligations.attempted: I reduced the requested guarantee to simultaneous inclusion estimation, randomized quadratic-form probing, and evaluation of a finite conditional-expectation ratio.  The first two are pointwise estimable, but converting them to the advertised uniform risk error and evaluating the conditional ratio in polynomial time remain unproved.
open_obligations.partial_result: The finite evaluator supplies an exact algorithm by enumeration, and Monte Carlo draws from \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) can estimate each \(\pi_u\) and every bilinear form \(x^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_Gx\) pointwise.  What is not proved is a polynomial sample bound uniform over all \(2n\) inclusion probabilities and the operator norm at the relative accuracy needed when \(k/n\asymp\log(d)/d^2\), nor a polynomial procedure for the conditional Rao--Blackwell ratio (8).  In particular, an additive entrywise Monte Carlo guarantee does not imply an \(o(r(n,d))\) worst-case quadratic-form error over the endpoint \(L^2\) ball; that conversion would require operator-norm error \(o(nr(n,d))\).
